```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
```

```{r}
# Here I cleaned the Dataset to manipulate more easily.

df <- read_csv("Text_Extraction.csv")

colnames(df) <- c("Horodateur", "Society", "Paragraph", "Source", "Page", "Comment")
df <- df %>% select(Society, Paragraph, Source, Page, Comment)

df <- df %>%
  drop_na(Page) %>%
  arrange(Source, Page)
```

```{r}
# With this function I grouped the different document together and after, I grouped in the same lign the document with the pages that are consecutive. 

fusion_par_consecutivite <- function(group) {
  group <- group %>%
    mutate(
      Page = str_extract(as.character(Page), "\\d+"),         
      Page = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Page))               
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Page)) %>%
    arrange(Page)

  if (nrow(group) == 0) return(tibble())

  blocs <- list()
  bloc <- list(group[1, , drop = FALSE])

 for (i in 2:nrow(group)) {
  curr <- group[i, , drop = FALSE]
  prev <- group[i - 1, , drop = FALSE]

  if (nrow(curr) == 0 || nrow(prev) == 0) next

  curr_page <- curr$Page[[1]]
  prev_page <- prev$Page[[1]]

  if (is.na(curr_page) || is.na(prev_page)) {
    blocs <- append(blocs, list(bind_rows(bloc)))
    bloc <- list(curr)
    next
  }

  if (curr_page <= prev_page + 1) {
    bloc <- append(bloc, list(curr))
  } else {
    blocs <- append(blocs, list(bind_rows(bloc)))
    bloc <- list(curr)
  }
}


  blocs <- append(blocs, list(bind_rows(bloc)))

  fusionnes <- lapply(blocs, function(df_bloc) {
    tibble(
      Source = df_bloc$Source[1],
      Society = df_bloc$Society[1],
      Pages = paste(df_bloc$Page, collapse = ", "),
      Report = paste(df_bloc$Paragraph, collapse = "\n\n"),
      Comments = paste(na.omit(df_bloc$Comment), collapse = " | ")
    )
  })

  bind_rows(fusionnes)
}

# Apply the function to all the dataframe.

resultat <- df %>%
  group_by(Source) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  lapply(fusion_par_consecutivite) %>%
  bind_rows()

resultat_clean <- resultat %>% drop_na()
```

```{r}
write_csv(resultat_clean, "Data_Manipulation_R.csv")
print(resultat_clean)
```

```{r}
# Finally I can add a column with the size of each paragraph by putting the number of word in each paragraph.

resultat_clean <- resultat_clean %>%
  mutate(Word_Count = str_count(Report, "\\S+"))
```

```{r}
write_csv(resultat_clean, "Data_Manipulation _Fin_R.csv")
```

# Now let's proceed to the NLP task.

```{r}
resultat_clean <- read_csv("Data_Manipulation _Fin_R.csv")
```

```{r}
mfd <- read_csv("eMFD_wordlist.csv")
```

```{r}
 # Here we perform all the text preprocessing tasks, I convert everything to lowercase, tokenize the text, then filter to focus only on the first 50 rows. The inner join allows me to match each word with its entry in the dictionary and thus retrieve its score for the 5 moral categories in that dictionary.

mfd_clean <- mfd %>%
  mutate(word = tolower(word))

df_sample <- resultat_clean %>%
  slice(1:50) %>%
  mutate(id = row_number())

tokens <- df_sample %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, Report) %>%
  mutate(word = tolower(word))

joined <- tokens %>%
  inner_join(mfd_clean, by = "word")
```

```{r}
# Here, I calculate the moral score of each report. At the end, I chose to display  the categorie that have the highest score.

moral_scores <- joined %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    care = sum(care_p, na.rm = TRUE),
    fairness = sum(fairness_p, na.rm = TRUE),
    loyalty = sum(loyalty_p, na.rm = TRUE),
    authority = sum(authority_p, na.rm = TRUE),
    sanctity = sum(sanctity_p, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

moral_categories <- moral_scores %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    category = c("care", "fairness", "loyalty", "authority", "sanctity")[which.max(c(care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity))]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(id, category)

df_result <- df_sample %>%
  left_join(moral_categories, by = "id")
```

```{r}
write_csv(df_result, "Test_NLP_V2.csv")
print(df_result)
```
